title: Compact-support base change over a finite extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $I=(\varpi)$, using the adic datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$
be a compact-support base-change square [def-cbc-compact-support-square], with $f$ separated of finite type. Require that all four schemes are noetherian and finite-dimensional and that $\ell$ is invertible on them. No smoothness, properness or finite-type hypothesis on $g$ is imposed.

Write $\mathcal C_T=\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ for the completed integral category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and use its raw rationalization $\Dbc(T,E)=\mathcal C_T[1/\varpi]$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. The integral operations are completed pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and compact-support direct image $Rf_!=Rp_*j_!$ for a compactification of $f$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification], and their base-changed versions. On the rational categories use their $E$-linear extensions [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. Define the rational compact-support exchange to be the extension of the specified completed integral exchange [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map]. Then for every $K\in\Dbc(X,E)$ its component is an isomorphism
$$
\Ex_{!,E}(K):Lg^*Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!Lg'^*K
\quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y',E).
$$
It is natural in every rational morphism. For integral representatives $M,N$ equipped with a rational isomorphism identifying them, the two components agree under the isomorphisms induced by the two composite functors; this is independence of the integral lattice. Identity and pasted-square coherence hold for squares whose schemes lie in the stated category domains.

proof.text: By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $f'$ is separated of finite type. Apply [lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction] to $f$ and $f'$ with the compactifications of [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. All source and target schemes have its required domain hypotheses. This gives exact $A$-linear compact-support functors on the stated integral categories. The opens are quasi-compact: their sources are noetherian, and each inverse image of an affine open is an open subspace of that source.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; integral constructible landing and scalar-localization argument made explicit

proof.text: For every $M\in\mathcal C_T$ on any of the four corners, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] gives an interval $[a,b]$ containing its cohomology. Apply [lem-cbc-finite-extension-reduction-cone-bound] to this completed-module object. Its canonical quotient reductions therefore have the common cohomological interval $[a-1,b]$, independently of the exponent. This applies to every integral object, including the compact-support images obtained in step 1.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; integral constructible landing and scalar-localization argument made explicit

proof.text: For $u:T'\to T$ equal to either horizontal map, specialize [prop-weil-pbc-preservation-constructible] to $X=Y=T$, $X'=Y'=T'$, vertical maps the identities and both horizontal maps $u$. This square is cartesian; the identities are proper with fibres empty or points, so take $e=0$. Take $N=\ell$: the residue field $A/I$ has characteristic $\ell$, so $N(A/I)=0$, and $N$ is invertible on both schemes. Step 2 supplies its common reduction interval for every input. The theorem's third conclusion gives $Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}M\in\mathcal C_{T'}$.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; integral constructible landing and scalar-localization argument made explicit

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-completed-pullback-triangles], the specified completed pullback preserves shifts and ambient distinguished triangles of complete objects. Its additivity and $A$-linearity on these complete categories are exactly the assertions of [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange]. Step 3 gives constructible landing. The full categories have inherited shifts and triangles by [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated], so the ambient shift comparisons and distinguished triangles restrict. Thus the two completed pullbacks are exact $A$-linear functors on the stated categories. Together with step 1 this defines the two exact $A$-linear composites $F=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_!$ and $G=Rf'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; integral constructible landing and scalar-localization argument made explicit

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], the raw rational category has the same objects as its integral category. Thus regard $K$ as an integral object $K_0\in\mathcal C_X$, without any lattice-existence assertion. By [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], $K_0$ is derived $I$-complete and its reductions have compatible etale-origin witnesses. The adic datum and compact-support square are assumed, so [thm-cbc-complete-proetale] applies and gives the specified integral exchange $\eta_{K_0}:F(K_0)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(K_0)$, where $F=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_!$ and $G=Rf'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$. Its endpoints belong to $\mathcal C_{Y'}$ by steps 1–4. Since this is a full subcategory, the ambient inverse is a morphism in it and still satisfies both inverse equations. It is natural and coherent for identities and pasted squares as asserted by that theorem.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; integral constructible landing and scalar-localization argument made explicit

proof.text: Apply the general functor-and-transformation assertion of [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] to the four exact $A$-linear integral functors and to $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$. This gives the rational functors and the extended exchange with component $\eta_{K_0}\otimes1$. It is the displayed exchange by its definition in the statement. The extension of a composite agrees with the composite of extensions: for a pure tensor $u\otimes a$ both send it to $F_1(F_2(u))\otimes a$, since the extensions are $E$-linear and agree on integral maps. Such pure tensors generate each Hom module by [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Thus the transformation has exactly the indicated source and target functors.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; integral constructible landing and scalar-localization argument made explicit

proof.text:
Let $v=\eta_{K_0}^{-1}$. The composition and identity formulas of [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] give
$$(v\otimes1)\circ(\eta_{K_0}\otimes1)=(v\circ\eta_{K_0})\otimes1=\mathrm{id}\otimes1,$$
while $(\eta_{K_0}\otimes1)\circ(v\otimes1)=(\eta_{K_0}\circ v)\otimes1=\mathrm{id}\otimes1$. Hence $v\otimes1$ is an inverse in the raw rational category on $Y'$, proving the claimed isomorphism for every $K$.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; integral constructible landing and scalar-localization argument made explicit

proof.text: Write $F_E,G_E$ for the rational composites. Integral naturality says $G(u)\eta_M=\eta_NF(u)$ for an integral map $u:M\to N$. Using the bilinear composition of [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], tensoring this equation with $a\in E$ gives $G_E(u\otimes a)(\eta_M\otimes1)=(\eta_N\otimes1)F_E(u\otimes a)$. By addition it holds for every rational map, including a rational isomorphism $h:M\to N$ specifying the identification of two integral representatives. Since a functor sends inverse pairs to inverse pairs, $F_E(h)$ and $G_E(h)$ are isomorphisms. The equation therefore identifies the two components under precisely these induced identifications, proving lattice independence without requiring an integral lift of $h$.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; integral constructible landing and scalar-localization argument made explicit

proof.text: The integral identity and pasting diagrams commute by [thm-cbc-complete-proetale]. Apply the localization functor $Q$ to every component and comparison in those diagrams. By [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], $Q(vu)=Q(v)Q(u)$ and $Q(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. Step 6 identifies the rational composite functors with the extensions of the integral composites. Whiskering is also respected: if $H$ is one of the integral functors and $t$ a comparison component, its rational extension satisfies $H_E(Q(t))=Q(H(t))$ by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. Therefore every edge and every path in a rational identity or pasting diagram is the image of its integral counterpart. The integral equalities remain equalities after $Q$, giving the claimed coherence for all identity and pasted squares within the stated category domains.
